scope: Current domain-neutral AI generation method and actual two Round1 provider transports, read-only

findings.status: Current production text-only approval scope; native visual orchestration gate is sufficient for this run
findings.observedDefect: review() supplies original source access, bound plan context, Markdown and structural findings, but no rendered artifact or image pin. REVIEW has one unqualified approved boolean. iteration accepts that boolean plus an empty structural list and stops without a visual/source-fidelity gate. The Round1 editor really received approved=true with no findings while its bound Markdown changed source h1 into h3, omitted the shared header, and added a nonexistent grid wrapper. Its text result was written at 21:59:32Z; the current layout PNG was written at 22:01:40Z. Renderer correctly reports semanticApproval NOT_ASSESSED, so display PASS cannot fill the missing approval scope.
findings.causeBoundary: The artifacts prove a text-only reviewer missed source-backed projection defects. They do not prove the reviewer's internal motive or that it read no shared layout through an indirect command. Review command strings explicitly include the Edit view and shared CSS; no command names _Layout.cshtml literally.
findings.genericFixForThisRun: Keep text approval separate. After real rendering, use a separate native AI review that reads the raw view/shared layout/CSS, the exact Markdown, and its pinned current images. Record reviewed image paths/hashes, document SHA, render-manifest SHA, source snapshot/reference mode, states/viewport coverage, source-backed findings and explicit unassessed limits. Do not select a completed screen when a major visual/source mismatch remains. Feed those source-backed findings into the next fresh analysis/writer round. No source application execution or business answer dictionary is needed.
findings.boundedProductionFollowup: Add explicit assessmentScope and visualFidelity NOT_ASSESSED to text review handoffs/statuses; require a separately bound visual-review artifact for a screen-complete approval policy. The core review may remain compatible as a text review. A provider image API redesign is unnecessary for the current native orchestration.
meaningfulChecks: Synthetic structurally valid text-approved screen missing a source-derived shared header must stay VISUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED until a separate visual review completes.
Synthetic source h1 changed to h3, invented class wrapper, or incompatible mode combined into one image must be rejected by independent source/image review, even when browser decoding succeeds.
Normal exact source projection with explicitly reviewed images and no major findings may complete.
Changing Markdown, layout PNG, render manifest, snapshot mode or image list after visual review must invalidate approval; approval for an old image cannot bind a fresh draft.

findings.status: Confirmed Round1 effective-input defect; current helper fixed, frozen Round2 runtime proposed by root
findings.observedDefect: All six preserved Round1 prompts have their provider-recorded prompt SHA verified and lack the current whole-plan map marker. They carry only the target document plan at launch. Current _document_context returns the exact source-derived original plan ID/path/title/kind/responsibilities map, but the newer source helper and its passing helper unit test do not retroactively change an existing imported orchestration process or saved prompt. Round1 review thus lacked authoritative related-document ID/path routing even though files were updated before later stages completed.
findings.causeBoundary: Effective prompt omission is directly verified. Stale imported runtime is consistent with all phases carrying the old context, but a process import timeline was not independently reconstructed here. No newer whole-plan context was falsely attributed to Round1.
findings.genericFixForThisRun: Start each revised run in a fresh process importing only the hash-pinned frozen runtime. Check loaded module __file__ paths and code hashes against the run manifest. Before launching analysis, writer and reviewer, validate the actual saved prompt/context carries the exact pinned whole-plan ID/path/title/kind/responsibility index, and record plan SHA plus context SHA. Abort before the provider call on mismatched effective context. Do not imply that a planned sibling has already been generated.
meaningfulChecks: Provider-spy integration test must inspect actual analysis, draft and review prompt inputs, not only _document_context output.
Changing a related document identity/path or the bound plan bytes must stop before provider launch.
Importing a workflow/prompts module outside the frozen runtime must fail the launch check, even when the live checkout has the intended source version.
Source-only and assisted runs must retain their distinct allowed material maps; related plan routing must not add evaluator expectations or generated-state claims.

secondaryScopeLimits: rendering.py:387,396 fixes both contexts at width1440/height1000. Round1 images therefore do not verify source-derived narrow-width media queries. Invented grid-wrapper behavior is a raw-source/DOM finding, not an observed narrow-viewport result. Optional future viewport coverage should be selected from AI source analysis and recorded without hardcoded business breakpoints.

Prompts already include shared-layout/CSS, no invented wrappers, separate incompatible modes, and no visual claim without viewed images (prompts.py:50-52,92). Their current presence was freshly checked; they were absent from preserved Round1 prompts. No further generic prose patch is proposed here.

Python remains transport/hash/structure/rendering. No mechanical business prose authoring was identified in these paths. Previously fixed relative-link preservation and provider interruption recording are outside these new findings.
